scenes.title: Hiker jumping back on a sunlit trail from a curved wooden root milliseconds before recognizing it — paired with LeDoux's Low-Road vs High-Road diagram
scenes.era: 1995, sunlit woodland trail & NYU Center for Neural Science chart

layout.description: Bright sunlit forest footpath where a dark S-curved oak root lies across sun-dappled gravel; in crisp documentary framing, a hiker mannequin recoils mid-step while a side-panel / studio bench displays Joseph LeDoux's two-arrow Thalamus -> Amygdala (Fast Blur) vs Thalamus -> Cortex -> Amygdala (Sharp Detail) schematic.

positions.who: Hiker mannequin (in khaki field shirt and hiking boots)
positions.where: caught mid-step recoiling one boot sharply backward from the curved wooden root on the sunlit path before leaning back in with relief
positions.facing: looking down at the S-curved root

positions.who: Joseph LeDoux (mannequin in NYU blazer and open shirt, studio/lab bench)
positions.where: pointing to the short direct lower arrow ('Low Road: Fast Blur') beating the tall upper cortical loop ('High Road: Sharp Bark Detail')

props.name: S-curved dark oak tree root on gravel path
props.period_detail: harmless deadwood branch whose silhouette mimics a coiled serpent in peripheral blur
props.physical_behavior: triggers Low-Road jump at 100 ms, resolved as harmless bark by High Road at 300 ms

props.name: blurry vs razor-sharp comparison frames
props.period_detail: two square photo plates on the lab bench: left plate blurred into a snake-like smudge (Low Road), right plate razor-sharp showing wood grain and twigs (High Road)
props.physical_behavior: shows exact resolution tradeoff for speed

props.name: Dual-Pathway Thalamus-Cortex-Amygdala board
props.period_detail: museum-clean anatomical diagram with two clean path lines
props.physical_behavior: illustrates why survival beats accuracy by 2x speed

actions.verb_sequence: spots dark S-curve peripherally -> boots recoil instantly BEFORE head finishes turning -> focuses clearly on the dry oak bark and exhales with a laugh
traces the short thalamus-to-amygdala shortcut beating the longer cortical loop

reactions.reaction: steps calmly over the harmless wooden root once the High Road all-clear lands
notes why 100 stick false-alarms beat missing 1 real viper

scenes.wardrobe: Clean khaki outdoor hiking shirt, canvas pack, and boots on hiker; dark NYU blazer and collared shirt on LeDoux.
scenes.lighting: Bright high-key sunlit woodland daylight & crisp studio bench illumination.
scenes.recognition_hook: Your boots leap backward off the trail BEFORE your eyes even realize the 'snake' is a crooked wooden branch — because your thalamus runs a secret two-speed race.

key_visual.description: a hiker mannequin recoiling mid-step from a snake-shaped wooden tree root on a sunlit path alongside a 'Fast Low Road vs Sharp High Road' thalamus-cortex-amygdala diagram

layout.description: High-key neurophysiology bench showing a millisecond spike trace with TWO distinct arrival peaks inside lateral amygdala: Peak 1 at 12 ms (Thalamic) and Peak 2 at ~28 ms (Cortical).

positions.where: pointing a pen tip to the crisp 12-ms early arrival spike on the monitor
alert inside a clean acoustic tone chamber

actions.verb_sequence: Peak 1 fires at 12 ms directly from thalamus -> Peak 2 arrives later from cortex

reactions.reaction: maps the monosynaptic lateral-amygdala front door

scenes.wardrobe: White lab coat; articulated matte-white porcelain rat sculpture.
